summary: Build programme pathways, indicators, and evaluation plans with practical exercises. Explore the five-day logic models and theory of change course.
lede: A logic model maps programme inputs, activities, outputs, and outcomes, while a theory of change explains the pathway and assumptions linking them. For programme designers, monitoring and evaluation specialists, and project leads, this course builds practical skills in mapping pathways, reviewing assumptions, selecting indicators, and planning evidence collection. It also uses OECD DAC criteria and Excel-based templates to structure evaluation questions, indicator matrices, and reporting.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who design, monitor, evaluate, or report on programmes and need to make outcome pathways and evidence plans more usable.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: No formal evaluation qualification is required. Familiarity with programme or project objectives is useful. Basic spreadsheet skills will help with the Excel-based indicator exercise; coding or programming is not required.
